football_evidence.question: Can Texas State win at the line of scrimmage?
football_evidence.assessment: No material disagreement: EdgeDesk and the line are within 0.2 points.
supporting: When Boise State has the ball (pass protection against the pass rush): Boise State’s offense has allowed a sack on 2.6% of its dropbacks, and Texas State’s defense sacks the quarterback on 3.1% of opponent dropbacks (FBS average 5.7%).

When Texas State has the ball (pass protection against the pass rush): Texas State’s offense has allowed a sack on 3.9% of its dropbacks, and Boise State’s defense sacks the quarterback on 10.3% of opponent dropbacks (FBS average 5.7%).

When Texas State has the ball (the line of scrimmage on running plays): Texas State’s offense is stopped at or behind the line on 13.7% of its runs, and Boise State’s defense stops 25.9% of opponent runs at or behind the line (FBS average 17.5%).
In his last two games (Colorado State and Utah State), Jackson averaged 6.7 yards per attempt, against 8.9 in his five games before that.
contradicting: When Boise State has the ball (big plays through the air): Boise State’s offense turns 9.2% of its pass plays into explosive gains, and Texas State’s defense gives up explosive gains on 8.0% of opponent pass plays (FBS average 10.2%).

When Boise State has the ball (big plays on the ground): Boise State’s offense turns 8.4% of its runs into explosive gains, and Texas State’s defense gives up explosive gains on 2.9% of opponent runs (FBS average 6.5%).
When Texas State has the ball (the run game against the run defense): Texas State’s offense averages 6.1 yards per carry, and Boise State’s defense allows 5.0 yards per carry (FBS average 5.0).

When Texas State has the ball (third down): Texas State’s offense converts 52.8% of its third downs, and Boise State’s defense allows opponents to convert 35.9% of their third downs (FBS average 39.5%).
quarterbacks: Maddux Madsen has completed 124 of 190 passes (65.3%) for 1,445 yards, 7.6 yards per attempt, 14 touchdowns and no interceptions in seven games for Boise State, and has been sacked on 5 of 195 dropbacks.

Brad Jackson has completed 133 of 195 passes (68.2%) for 1,606 yards, 8.2 yards per attempt, 14 touchdowns and 4 interceptions in seven games for Texas State, and has been sacked on 8 of 203 dropbacks.
